title: GMAT Focus Quant Practice Test 7
instructions: GMAT Focus Edition Quantitative Reasoning: 21 Problem Solving questions, 45 minutes. An on-screen calculator is permitted.

questions.prompt: A budget of £1,400.00 has 35% committed, and 40% of what remains is then committed. How much is uncommitted?
questions.explanation: After the first commitment £910.00 remains; committing 40% of that leaves £546.00. Subtracting both percentages from the original gives £350.00, which applies the second to the wrong base.

questions.prompt: A coach travels for 1.5 hours at 88 km/h and then 2.5 hours at 104 km/h. What is the average speed for the journey?
questions.explanation: Distance is 132 + 260 = 392 km over 4 hours, giving 98 km/h. The unweighted average of the two speeds is 96, which ignores the longer time at the higher speed.

questions.prompt: Two sums of money are in the ratio 5 : 9, and the larger exceeds the smaller by £156.00. What is their total?
questions.explanation: The difference is 4 parts, so one part is £156.00 / 4 = £39.00. The total is 14 parts, £546.00.

questions.prompt: £3,000.00 is invested at 5.5% a year, compounded annually. After how many whole years does it first exceed £4,000.00?
questions.explanation: The balance passes £4,000.00 between year 5 (£3,920.88) and year 6 (£4,136.53), so 6 whole years are needed.

questions.prompt: A lawn measures 20 m by 14 m. A path 1.5 m wide runs all the way around it. What is the area of the path?
questions.explanation: The outer rectangle is 23 by 17, an area of 391 m². Subtracting the lawn's 280 m² leaves 111 m². The path adds its width to both ends of each side, which is the step most often missed.

questions.prompt: A machine fails a test with probability 0.3 on any run, independently each time. What is the probability it fails at least once in three runs?
questions.explanation: It passes all three with probability 0.7³ = 34.3%, so it fails at least once with probability 65.7%. Adding 30% three times gives 90%, which double counts multiple failures.

questions.prompt: A shop sells an item for £84.00; a competitor sells it for £69.00. What percentage discount must the shop give to match the competitor?
questions.explanation: The reduction needed is £15.00, which as a percentage of its own price is 17.86%. Dividing by the competitor's price instead gives 21.74%.

questions.prompt: One group of 16 has a mean score of 72; another of 24 has a mean of 58. What is the mean of all 40?
questions.explanation: Total score is 16 × 72 + 24 × 58 = 2544, over 40 people: 63.6. The unweighted average of the two means is 65, too high because the larger group scored lower.

questions.prompt: One pipe fills a tank in 10 minutes and another in 15 minutes. Running together, how long do they take?
questions.explanation: Rates add: 1/10 + 1/15 = 1/6 of the tank a minute, so the tank fills in 6 minutes. Averaging the two times gives 12.5, which is longer than the faster pipe alone and cannot be right.

questions.prompt: Tax is charged at 20% on income above £12,570.00. What is the tax on an income of £38,500.00?
questions.explanation: Taxable income is £25,930.00, and 20% of that is £5,186.00. Taxing the whole income gives £7,700.00.

questions.prompt: What is the sum of the first 30 odd numbers?
questions.explanation: The first 30 odd numbers run 1, 3, 5 … 59, and their sum is 30² = 900. The same result comes from 30 × (1 + 59)/2.

questions.prompt: £1,500.00 is exchanged at 1.146 units per pound, with a 2% fee taken from the converted amount. How many units are received, to two decimal places?
questions.explanation: Converted: 1500 × 1.146 = 1719 units. After the 2% fee: 1684.62. Ignoring the fee gives 1719.

questions.prompt: A pack of 5 costs £3.45 and a pack of 8 costs £5.36. Which is cheaper per item, and by how much?
options: the pack of 5, by £0.02 an item
the pack of 8, by £0.05 an item
They cost the same per item
the pack of 8, by £0.02 an item
the pack of 8, by £0.15 an item
questions.correctAnswer: the pack of 8, by £0.02 an item
questions.explanation: Per item: £0.69 against £0.67, so the pack of 8 is cheaper by £0.02. The larger pack is not automatically the better value.

questions.prompt: After a 25% increase a rent is £800.00 a month. What was it before?
questions.explanation: The new rent is 125% of the old, so the old is £800.00 / 1.25 = £640.00. Taking 25% off the new figure gives £600.00, which is too low because the percentage belongs to the smaller base.

questions.prompt: How many integers from 1 to 300 inclusive are divisible by 4 or by 6?
questions.explanation: Multiples of 4: 75. Multiples of 6: 50. Multiples of both, that is of 12: 25. By inclusion and exclusion, 75 + 50 − 25 = 100.

questions.prompt: A road climbs 42 m over a horizontal distance of 600 m. What is the gradient as a percentage?
questions.explanation: Gradient is rise over run: 42/600 = 7%. Inverting the fraction gives 14.29, which is not a percentage at all.

questions.prompt: A partnership makes £96,000.00. One partner takes a salary of £24,000.00 first, and the remainder is split 3 : 5 between the two. What is the larger share of the remainder?
questions.explanation: After the salary, £72,000.00 remains. The larger share is 5 parts of 8: £45,000.00. Splitting the whole profit instead gives £60,000.00.

questions.prompt: A driver must cover 210 km in 3 hours but loses 30 minutes at the start. What average speed is needed over the remaining time?
questions.explanation: Only 2.5 hours remain for 210 km, so 210 / 2.5 = 84 km/h. The originally planned speed was 70 km/h.

questions.prompt: A machine costing £16,000.00 depreciates 20% a year on its reducing value. After 3 years it is sold for £9,000.00. What is the profit or loss against its book value?
questions.explanation: Book value is £16,000.00 × 0.8³ = £8,192.00. Selling at £9,000.00 gives a profit of £808.00 against that value.

questions.prompt: Of 240 staff, 35% work part time, and 60% of the part-time staff are women. How many part-time women are there?
questions.explanation: Part-time staff number 240 × 0.35 = 84, and 60% of those is 50.4. Taking 60% of all staff gives 144.

questions.prompt: £20,000.00 is invested for one year at 6%. How much more interest does monthly compounding earn than a single annual payment?
questions.explanation: Monthly compounding earns £1,233.56 against £1,200.00 paid annually, a difference of £33.56. Quoting the whole monthly figure rather than the difference is the trap.

answerKey.gmat-quant-007-q013: the pack of 8, by £0.02 an item
